subject: Re: Renewal — commit tilt analysis & prefetch optimization
messages:
From: Elliot Shaw <elliot@commitlytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + Q3 usage audit attached

Kimberly —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier this week. We finished an internal audit of our Q3 token usage and latency impact as we dial up features for the holiday release. Two flagged items: a) our chat endpoints have a heavier token tail than expected (system & assistant tokens) and b) latency-sensitive calls caused us to disable some batching for safety, which drove up cost.

I attached a CSV export (commitlytics_q3_usage.csv) and a short latency bench PDF (latency_bench.pdf). High level: run-rate is ~1.9B tokens/mo with 32% YOY spike in inference tokens; peak-hour concurrency drove retries that look like duplicated token spend. We're entering renewal in late Nov and need guidance on a staged path to increase committed capacity while keeping unit economics reasonable.

Can your team run a quick pass on prefetch/batching adjustments and quantify the expected token-savings if we move to a dedicated pool + prefix prefetching/kv cache?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

Elliot
Elliot Shaw
Head of Platform
Commitlytics

Attachments: commitlytics_q3_usage.csv (csv export), latency_bench.pdf (pdf, 4 pages)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot@commitlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal window + Q3 usage audit attached

Elliot —

Appreciate the context and the artifacts. Quick read-through notes below before we sync:
- Token mix: looks like ~45% system/instruction and 55% assistant/user tokens on average. That means savings from prefix caching could meaningfully reduce repeated system tokens for similar prompts.
- Retries: the CSV shows spikes correlated with a 120ms tail latency window. A modest batching + prefetch strategy should reduce tail and remove retry churn.
- Proposed immediate next step: we can run a small synthetic prefetch test (2–3 days) on a dedicated staging route and report token delta. If results look good, we propose a staged commit uplift (20% initial increase) with a 30-day monitoring window and automatic scale-back if token-economics worsen.

I'm free for a call tomorrow at 11am PT if that works. Ben — I pulled pricing examples from the playbook for a staged uplift and added them to a proposal draft (see Ben's note). Marissa — would you prefer we include SLA credit language on the initial uplift?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Elliot Shaw <elliot@commitlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Tiered commit proposal + math (draft)

Kim / Elliot —

I pulled together a short tiered commit proposal based on the Q3 run-rate. Highlights:
- Baseline run-rate: 1.9B tokens/mo.
- Recommended initial uplift: +20% commit (to cover runway + staging tests) -> effective commit 2.28B tokens/mo.
- Conditional second tranche: +15% after 30-day monitoring if token-econ improves (prefetch + batching validation).
- Estimated token-savings from prefetch/batching: 8–14% (conservative 8%).
- Net spend: with a conservative 8% token reduction, unit cost falls ~6.4% vs current on-demand mix; with 12% savings it's ~9.7% lower.

Attached is the draft pricing PDF with itemized tranches and sample DocuSign language for an addendum (tiered_commit_proposal.pdf). Elliot — if you can confirm expected peak concurrency windows and any strict latency SLOs, I’ll sharpen the SLA and pricing buckets.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Director — Redwood Inference

Attachment: tiered_commit_proposal.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tiered commit proposal + math (draft)

Team —

Quick internal note before we send a formal proposal:
- Risk: we need to ensure that the prefetched cache does not conflict with PII handling for Commitlytics (they flagged a narrow set of prompts that include hashed PII). Work with Security to validate prefetch rules for exclusion.
- Ops: recommend a 14-day stagger for the first tranche (not immediate full allocation), with telemetry hooks to our Console: token mix by route, tail latency percentile, retry rate, and a Post Mortem checkpoint at day 30.
- Approval: I'm comfortable with the 20% initial uplift if Security signs off and we include an SLA exit clause after 30 days.

I've dropped a short checklist in the shared drive for the renewal (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Commitlytics-renewal-checklist). Ben, please add the final pricing buckets. Kimberly, loop Security and the Solutions Eng lead on the prefetch rule set.

Marissa
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Shaw <elliot@commitlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal: staged uplift + prefetch pilot (proposal attached)

Elliot —

Thanks for the audit and for working through the details with us. Below is a concise proposal to move forward; attached is a one-page plan and a MOP workbook (mop_plan_v1.xlsx) for the pilot.

Proposal summary (actionable items):
1) Short pilot (14 days) on a dedicated staging route
   - Config: prefix prefetch enabled on non-PII routes, KV cache TTL = 10min, batching window = 20ms (optimistic) / 50ms (conservative fallback)
   - Goal: validate token-savings (target: >=8%) and reduce retry churn by 50% during peak windows
2) Commit structure (if pilot meets KPIs)
   - Tranche A: +20% commit for 30 days (billing applied immediately, monitoring window active)
   - Tranche B: optional +15% after 30-day validation (DocuSign addendum link: https://docusign.net/link/ABC123-mop)
3) Safeguards & SLA
   - Security exclusion: prefetch rules will exclude any route flagged by Commitlytics as containing PII. Security review to complete within 5 business days.
   - Exit: automatic scale-back and credit if token-econ degrades by >5% vs pilot baseline

Estimated impact (conservative):
- Projected token-savings: 8% -> puts effective run-rate at ~2.10B tokens/mo for Tranche A vs 2.28B gross commit (net savings baked into renewal math).
- Cost delta: projected ~6–7% unit cost improvement in month 1; further improvements expected post-tranche B if batching settings are relaxed safely.

Next steps: confirm pilot start date (we're available 10/25 or 10/26), Security contact (name/email), and an internal sample of 10 example prompts for prefetch-rule validation.

Thanks — we’ll finalize the DocuSign and the MOP once you confirm dates.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Attachments: mop_plan_v1.xlsx (xlsx workbook, 6 sheets), tiered_commit_proposal.pdf (previous draft referenced)
